we have introduced a novel task, language-driven image generation; that we have implemented a simple, effective, method for performing this task; and that we have shown that the method is sufficient to generate images that capture the semantic content of a word embedding and that are sufficient to discriminate among different concepts.
we introduce language-driven image synthesis, a novel task in computer vision, and show that a simple method is sufficient to generate images that are interpretable and useful in a variety of tasks.

(1) we can generate natural images from word embeddings, (2) our method can produce images that are semantically meaningful, (3) we can generate images of specific categories, (4) we can generate specific images for a given word, and (5) the images are interpretable by humans, i.e., they are not random or meaningless, but they do not capture fine-grained details of objects.
